answer: An optical scattering protocol curbs Sybil attacks by measuring speckle patterns created when a violet laser probes an unclonable timber fiber tag on each node. Verifiers evaluate refraction angles against physical baselines to confirm hardware uniqueness. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of fabricating discrete physical optical tags per identity rather than instantiating virtual clones. However, humidity shifts can warp the fiber substrate in an outdoor dune, causing false rejections.
